about: A medieval Marian antiphon, sung at the end of Compline through the long season after Pentecost, and since Leo XIII said after low Mass as well, following the threefold Ave María. The first half is nothing but address: the prayer opens on its verb — Salve — and pours five vocative names after it: Queen, Mother, life, sweetness, hope. The prayer does not hide where the speaker stands: it calls us the banished children of Eve in a valley of tears. After the antiphon come a versicle and its answer, by which priest and people pass on to prayer.

s01.translation: Hail, holy Queen, Mother of mercy, our life, our sweetness and our hope.

s02.translation: To thee do we cry, poor banished children of Eve.

s03.translation: To thee do we send up our sighs, mourning and weeping in this valley of tears.

s04.translation: Turn, then, most gracious Advocate, thine eyes of mercy toward us.

s05.translation: And after this our exile show unto us the blessed fruit of thy womb, Jesus.

s06.translation: O clement, O loving, O sweet Virgin Mary.

s07.translation: Pray for us, O holy Mother of God.

s08.translation: That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

w001.function: Not an interjection but an imperative: the verb sálveo means to be in health, and the Roman greeting says literally “be well”.

w004.function: Genitive depending on “Mater” (w003) — the Mother who bears mercy and gives it out.

w008.function: The fifth vocative — the genitive “misericórdiæ” (w004) stands among them — and the verb of this sentence is the “Salve” (w001) that opened it.

w010.function: Repeated at the end of the sentence: the greeting closes round the whole string of names like a clasp.

w014.function: A noun in the nominative, in apposition to the “we” carried inside “clamámus” (w013) — we are the exiles.

w020.function: A participle in the nominative plural, agreeing with the subject carried inside “suspirámus” (w019).

w025.function: Genitive plural depending on “valle” (w026): a valley belonging to tears, a valley that tears fill.

w027.function: An interjection of urging, and the hinge of the prayer: it passes from complaint to petition.

w031.function: A demonstrative set before its noun: not any eyes, but those known ones — those merciful eyes of thine.

w048.function: The second petition to the Mother — the fourth imperative addressed to her — and the point of the whole prayer: it does not ask to be taken out of the valley, but that she show her Son.

w062.function: Vocative. The corpus spells genetrix with an e, as it does everywhere; both spellings are the same word, from gigno, to beget.

w065.function: Passive: literally “that we may be made worthy”. The worthiness is not our own doing.

w066.function: Ablative: “dignus” takes what one is worthy of in the ablative. The word depends on “digni” (w064), not on the verb.
